title: Fourth of July fireworks celebrations in Volusia, Flagler for U.S. 250 - NewsBreak
text:
By Sheldon Gardner Brenno Carillo ,
19 hours ago It's not your typical Fourth of July. This year, the country celebrates its 250th birthday , also called the semiquincentennial.
Gov. Ron DeSantis , in giving state workers more time off for the special occasion, called it a time to celebrate and "spend time with family and friends honoring the blessings of liberty that generations of Americans have fought to preserve.”
DeSantis said in a June news release , “America’s 250th anniversary is a historic milestone and an opportunity to reflect on the courage, sacrifice, and enduring principles that established the United States as the freest and most prosperous nation in the world."
Across Volusia and Flagler counties, people have many options for enjoying fireworks this holiday weekend. Here's a look at what's ahead.
Daytona Beach Alter Eagles, and Eagles tribute band, will perform at the Daytona Beach Bandshell beginning at at 7:15 p.m. on July Fourth, and fireworks will follow at 9:45 p.m. The concert is free.
DeBary " Freedom Fest " will take place from 5-10:30 p.m. on July Fourth at Gemini Springs Park at 37 Dirksen Drive in DeBary. The fireworks, drone and laser show will start at 9 p.m.
DeLand The " Firecracker Festival " will be from 6-9 p.m. on July 3 at Earl Brown Park at 751 S. Alabama Ave. in DeLand. A fireworks display is planned at dusk. Bring your own lawn chairs.
Deltona The "United We Celebrate 250 Years" event will be start at 5 p.m. on July Fourth at Dewey O. Boster Park at 1200 Saxon Blvd. in Deltona. Fireworks will start around 9:15 p.m. The event will include live music, food vendors, rides, face painting, bounce houses and a BMX stunt show. Bring your own lawn chairs.
Edgewater Edgewater's Fourth of July celebration will be from 6-10 p.m. on July 4 at Menard May Park at 413 S. Riverside Drive and Kennedy Park at 103 N. Riverside Drive in Edgewater. Fireworks are planned at dusk. The event will include live music, food trucks and other activities. Bring your own lawn chair.
New Smyrna Beach New Smyrna Beach's celebration will be from 4 to about 9:30 p.m. on July Fourth at Riverside Park, 299 S. Riverside Drive, New Smyrna Beach. Fireworks will start at 9:15 p.m.
Ormond Beach Ormond Beach will host a July 4 celebration from 8-9:30 p.m. on July Fourth at Rockefeller Gardens, 26 Riverside Drive in Ormond Beach. Fireworks will start at 9 p.m.
Port Orange Port Orange's " 4th of July Spectacular " will be from 5:30 to 9:30 p.m. on July Fourth at the City Center Municipal Complex at 1000 City Center Circle in Port Orange. The fireworks and drones show will start at 9 p.m. The event will include a classic car show, live music and a pie-baking competition.
Flagler County and its communities, including Palm Coast, Flagler Beach and Bunnell, have several Fourth of July celebrations planned for the weekend.
Flagler Beach The city's recurrent First Friday event is planned for July 3, at Veterans Park in Flagler Beach, and will include food, music and family fun.
The event begins at 6 p.m. Veterans Park is located between Moody Boulevard and 2nd Street in downtown Flagler Beach.
To kick off celebration on July 4, the Rotary Club of Flagler Beach will present its Stars and Stripes parade starting at 9 a.m.
The parade will follow its traditional route along State Road A1A in Flagler Beach, traveling from 6th Street North to 6th Street South.
Palm Coast The weekend’s main event will be massive firework celebration at the Flagler Executive Airport, 201 Airport Road, Palm Coast.
The “Fireworks Over the Runways” event will feature a wide variety of food trucks, vendors, a beer garden, children’s activities, and live entertainment on the main stage, according to officials.
Gates will open at 5 p.m.
Following a performance of the national anthem, local dignitaries and elected officials will deliver a reading of the Declaration of Independence at 6:30 p.m.
At 7 p.m., “spectators can cheer on contestants in the first-ever "United Flagler Fourth Hot Dog Eating Competition," presented by Hot Diggity Dogs & Shakes, as local leaders and community personalities compete for the coveted title of ‘Top Dog.’”
A “spectacular fireworks display” is scheduled to follow at 9 p.m. Guests are encouraged to bring lawn chairs.
In addition, “this year’s event will feature a thrilling warbird showcase at the airport from 7 to 8 p.m., leading up to the fireworks finale,” officials said.
For more information, visit palmcoast.gov/events/home/details/unitedflagler4th.
— Sheldon Gardner covers Volusia County government, including Volusia County beaches, the city of Daytona Beach and local governments in West Volusia . Brenno Carillo is a local government reporter covering Flagler County, including Palm Coast and Flagler Beach, for The Daytona Beach News-Journal
